Fixture: 54_vardct_mixed_rgb_128x128_nofilters_d1.jxl
128x128 RGB, VarDCT lossy, gaborish and EPF disabled, d=1.0

Purpose
-------
The RGB counterpart to 50: same varblock-zoo intent (smooth ramp / 1px
checkerboard split, see below), gaborish and EPF disabled, d=1.0.

--gaborish=0 --epf=0 disables both restoration filters. Per 18181-3 Annex A
Table A.1:

    Part 3 error class:  peak <= 0.004,  RMSE <= 1e-5   (no filters)

Grading is against a reference DECODE of this stream, never against the
original source PNM -- see 50's sidecar for the full rationale (this applies
identically here). JPXL's own decoder cannot decode VarDCT yet; this fixture
is not wired into any decode test yet (wave 3 / 8F's tests/e2e_vardct.rs).

Provenance
----------

  libjxl rev:   196a43d996aa6ed33ebf98812a7c6d43b2b6d01b (v0.12-snapshot-2-g196a43d9)
  cjxl flags:   -d 1.0 --gaborish=0 --epf=0 -e 7
  Built by:     tools/setup-oracles.sh (flags recorded in
                tools/oracle-bin/PINNED_REVISIONS.txt)
  Regenerate:   tools/make-vardct-fixtures.sh
                That script IS the recipe; it rewrites the source and re-encodes.

  Source image: tests/fixtures/generated/src_vardct_mixed_rgb_128x128.ppm  (49167 bytes)
                sha256 35af85cc2cc50771ec10ec8842673a4fdc534e8eaa29d5153d313b34f4e8c85d
                Synthetic, written by the Python snippet inside
                tools/make-vardct-fixtures.sh -- no third-party image was
                used, converted or consulted. 128x128 8-bit RGB:
                  x <  64: R = x * 255 / 63, G = y * 255 / 127, B = (x+y) mod 256  smooth
                  x >= 64: magenta (255,0,255) / cyan (0,255,255), alternating
                           every pixel by (x+y) parity                 1px checkerboard

  Fixture:      2342 bytes
                sha256 a9b2de37977a42b159b8784a14825c77e63bf354f6df8bc17343b7d455017656

    tools/oracle-bin/djxl --output_format npy \
      tests/fixtures/handmade/54_vardct_mixed_rgb_128x128_nofilters_d1.jxl \
      /tmp/54.npy
  sha256 (pinned decoder, tools/oracle-bin/PINNED_REVISIONS.txt):
    7cc30c9380a334dd5d25426b562f0fa53a2893e4a030ed257be54c28aa872b1f
  Shape (1, 128, 128, 3) little-endian f32, per 18181-3 4.1.2. Decode is
  deterministic per libjxl revision, so this hash is expected to reproduce
  exactly on the pinned oracle build.

cjxl/djxl are used strictly as BLACK BOXES: they emit/consume conformant
streams for JPXL to parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a
different libjxl revision changes these digests, that is the point of
recording them -- do not silently update them; note the revision change.
